intro.en: Age 18. You join the degree college in town and share a hostel room with Chintu. Amma gives you your first smartphone. Somewhere on that phone, {cast:tempter} is waiting.

objective.en: First day at the town college. Find the admission desk.

text.en: The fee is ₹38,000 a year. Nanna's cotton money covers half. The clerk shows you three ways to pay the rest.

label.en: Apply for the state scholarship and work evenings at the delivery hub

outcome.en: The scholarship pays the fee. The hub pays ₹4,000 a month for 3 hours an evening. You learn to sleep on buses.

why.en: Free money first (scholarships), earned money second, borrowed money last.

label.en: Take a bank [[education_loan]], to repay after you get a job

outcome.en: The bank pays the college directly. Repayment starts after your course. You can focus on studying.

why.en: An education loan is 'good debt' if it raises your income. It's cheap (about 9.5%) and waits until you earn.

label.en: Borrow ₹20,000 from Narsaiah sahukar. It's quick

warn.en: A bank education loan costs about 9.5% a year and waits until you have a job. The [[sahukar]] charges 24% from day one, and adds it every month.

outcome.en: Narsaiah counts out the notes and opens his red ledger. "Study well, beta. I'll be here every month."

why.en: Quick money is usually the most expensive money. Always compare the yearly interest rate.

objective.en: Back to the hostel. Chintu has 'big news'.

text.en: Chintu shows you a Telegram channel: "LUCKY PRAKASH CAPITAL. 30% a month GUARANTEED. 2 lakh members." Lamborghini photos. VIP tips: ₹5,000. "Bro, it's {cast:tempter}! From our village!"

warn.en: 30% a month would turn ₹10,000 into ₹1.2 crore in 3 years. Nobody can guarantee that. Real advisers are SEBI-registered and never promise returns.

outcome.en: Welcome to VIP! Your first message arrives at 2 a.m.: "BIG TIP COMING. KEEP CASH READY."

why.en: Guaranteed high returns are the clearest sign of a scam. Risk and return always travel together.

label.en: Check SEBI's website: is he a registered adviser?

outcome.en: Not registered. The 'Lamborghini' is from a Dubai car show. You screenshot everything, and show Chintu.

why.en: Anyone giving investment advice for money must be SEBI-registered. Checking takes two minutes.

label.en: Ignore it and go to class

outcome.en: You go to class. Chintu joins VIP. Every night, his phone glows green and red.

why.en: Ignoring a scam keeps you safe. Warning your friends keeps them safe too.

objective.en: A VIP message just arrived. Open your phone (press P).

text.en: VIP tip: "Buy Spark Mobile shares NOW, they'll go 5x!" Then a private message: "Earn ₹5,000 a month! Just let us route trading profits through your bank account. 100% legal, bro."

label.en: Rent them your account for ₹5,000 a month

warn.en: Letting strangers move money through your account makes you a [[money_mule]]. That money is stolen from scam victims. Your account gets frozen and YOU face the police case.

outcome.en: ₹5,000 arrives on the first of every month. So do strange credits of ₹40,000, ₹75,000, ₹1,20,000... and debits, minutes later.

why.en: Mule accounts are how stolen money disappears. The account holder is the one the police find first.

label.en: Just buy the Spark Mobile tip with ₹5,000

outcome.en: Spark Mobile jumps 20% in a day. The VIP group cheers. You don't know the admins are selling to you.

why.en: In 'pump and dump' tips, the group buys first, tells you to buy, then sells to you at the top.

label.en: Leave the group and report it on the cyber-crime portal

outcome.en: You save every screenshot and report the channel. VIP money lost: ₹5,000. Lesson learned: priceless.

why.en: Reporting helps the police connect complaints. Your evidence may matter later.

objective.en: The bank called. Come immediately: your account is frozen.

text.en: Two cyber-police officers are waiting at the bank. Your account moved ₹8,40,000 of scam money in three months. {cast:banker} looks at you like she doesn't know you.

label.en: Tell the police everything and hand over the chats

outcome.en: Your chats lead the police to a call centre in Hyderabad. You're let off with a warning, and your account stays frozen for a year.

why.en: If you are ever used as a mule, stop, report and cooperate. It's the only way out.

label.en: Say you know nothing about it

warn.en: Lying to the police in a fraud case makes you look like part of the gang. Telling the truth is your only way out.

outcome.en: The chats are on your phone anyway. You're named in the charge sheet as an accused.

why.en: A money-mule case can mean arrest, a criminal record, and no bank account for years.

objective.en: Kavitha akka has opened a mutual fund desk. Go to the bank.

text.en: {cast:banker}: "A [[sip]] puts a fixed amount into a [[mutual_fund]] every month. An [[index_fund]] just buys India's top 50 companies. Low fee, no star manager." You have about ₹1,000 a month spare.

label.en: Start a ₹1,000 SIP in the Top-50 Index Fund

outcome.en: Your first units! ₹1,000 buys 9.6 units. Next month, the same ₹1,000 buys whatever the price allows.

why.en: Starting at 20 instead of 30 can nearly double what you have at 50. Time does the heavy lifting.

label.en: Pick the 'Star Active Fund': 40% return last year!

outcome.en: The star fund's brochure is very shiny. Its 1.8% yearly fee is in very small print.

why.en: Last year's star rarely repeats. A high [[expense_ratio]] is charged every year, good or bad.

label.en: Shares are scary. Put it in an FD

outcome.en: Safe and boring. The FD grows about 7% a year, just above rising prices.

why.en: FDs are great for money you need soon. For money you won't touch for 10+ years, growth funds usually do better.

label.en: Spend it. You're only young once

outcome.en: Biryani Fridays, new shoes, movie nights. Fun! In 30 years, that ₹1,000 a month could have been ₹20 lakh.

why.en: The cost of starting late is huge, because the earliest rupees have the longest time to grow.

objective.en: Breaking news on your phone! Open it (press P).

text.en: Markets fall 22% in a month. Spark Mobile falls 70%: the VIP admins sold at the top. Chintu is crying in the hostel corridor. Everyone says: "Sell before it goes to zero!"

label.en: Do nothing. Keep the SIP running

outcome.en: You delete the market app for a month. Your SIP keeps buying, now at lower prices.

why.en: Crashes are normal. Selling turns a temporary fall into a permanent loss. SIPs buy more units when prices are low.

label.en: Invest ₹2,000 more while prices are low

outcome.en: Your ₹2,000 buys 30% more units than last month. Kavitha akka nods: "Sale season."

why.en: For long-term money, a crash is a sale. Only invest money you won't need for years.

outcome.en: You sell at the bottom. Eight months later, the market is back up. You aren't in it.

why.en: Panic selling locks in the loss. Markets have always recovered; panicked investors often don't.

text.en: Your screenshots get Lucky Prakash Capital banned from Telegram. Forty students get their money back from the bank. Chintu still owes you a biryani.
You held through the crash. By graduation your SIP is back in the green, and you've learned the hardest investing skill: doing nothing when everyone panics.
You graduate safe, with a degree and a little money. You didn't lose much, but you didn't grow much either.
You sold in the crash and watched the recovery from outside. Chintu, who held, gets his money back. You swear off markets. That's the real loss.
No case, but a police record, a frozen account and a family that looks at you differently. Every bank form now asks a question you hate answering.
You are named as an accused in a ₹40 crore fraud case. You miss your final exams for court dates. Lucky Prakash's photo is nowhere in the file.
